title: Which is better, multiple maps or extra switches/variables/common-events?

posts.author: CreatureCola
posts.body:
Curious which is better in the long run for functionality and lag prevention.
I'm just wondering which of the two i should go with, would making duplicate maps of any place with houses to switch the doors to not be able to open during a specific day of the week, (market day) or use switches/variables/common events to control each of the doors? i feel like duplicating completed maps and just changing the door events would be the easiest way, but i don't want to do that if its harder on the system than setting up additional switches/variables, ect.
There would be roughly 7 duplicate maps in my game if i did it this way.
I can't set the door's page to directly link to a day variable because it asks for a number OR HIGHER meaning any days past it during the week would still function the same unless i changed it to sunday ( variable day 7 )or added extra switches/pages and conditional branches, so doing different maps feels easier? because i can say = exact number in the original condition- go to x map, else go to other map. without all the extra pages and what not. make sense?
The doors are already setup in a way to only be enterable between certain hours calculated by total minutes in a day, which also changes the page based off how much someone likes you ( can stay later, and can enter when they're not home, ect )
People have suggested doing this with dungeons at night to spawn different monsters, and that would be WAY more maps than doing it just for maps with houses/doors. My forest "dungeon" alone has 40 total floors and i'm planning 4 full sized dungeons (160 maps total, x2? ) would /that/ cause serious lag? only 2 of those dungeons are fully outside, so i suppose the other 2 don't need night time spawns. so about 80 x2. *shrug*

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
the number of maps has nothing to do with lag, because only one map is loaded at any given time.
ev3en the number of events on a map has limited effect on lag - the only events that can cause a lot of lag are badly structured parallel process events, and those have nothing to do with mapping.
the question on when a duplicate map is better and when a number of different event is better depends completely on the map - and simply adding another page to a door event to block that door when a certain switch is ON is not enough to warrant a duplicate map.
duplicate maps are more for differtent cutscenes with many moving events and similar cases where the map would get confusing if too many events need to behave differently.
or for your own example of using different map properties like different encounter tables.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
CreatureCola said:
Curious which is better in the long run for functionality and lag prevention.
Click to expand...
Nothing you describe here has anything effect on your game's functionality, nor any effect on lag.
It's entirely organizational for you within your project.
Lag is caused by your processor having to work hard. Things in an RPG Maker game which can cause that:
- Too many Autorun or parallel events doing too much stuff with no Wait
- Loading large files
Merely
having
a file (a map, an image, a plugin, whatever) in your project does absolutely nothing. It sits there on your hard drive.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
as I already wrote above, only parallel process events can add significantly to the lag. and it doesn't matter if those are with content or empty - so yes, and empty parallel process is bad.
anything else (like an empty action button event) is simply a decoration and you can add hundreds of them.

Please read what people have already written.
Technically, yes data must be used to know that an event is there, but it is so negligible that it's not something you should care about.
Now, the editor sometimes has a hard time coping with a lot of events on a map, but we are talking when you get into 1k+ events on a map.
None of this sounds like it will cause lag, but sounds disorganized and a poor way of managing your project. You may want to consider using common events to create "event folders" and better utilize the tools available for structuring logical flow to reduce redundant switches, variables, maps, and events.
As the professor of my (failed) programming course said:
If you find yourself writing the same function many times, there is probably a more efficient way of handling it.
